redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__invariants.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 2 of 123 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - iv18g (house FAIL), iv18h (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 121/123 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py: manifest_revalidated's per-commit 'the manifest this commit recorded does NOT validate' breach now appends a write-provenance clause. _commit_committer_moment(git_root, sha) reads the commit's committer time via `git log --format=%cI`, parsed through usage_ledger.parse_ts (re-exported from _usage_core) so it compares on the same epoch-seconds scale _journal_io.row_moment uses. _index_journal_target(git_root, index_rel, project) restates the git-root-relative index path the way a journal row's `target` names it (project-relative, since project need not equal git_root under meta.gitRoot). _last_index_write(project, target, before) reads the journal through _journal_io.read_all (the one reader, no second parser), filters rows by _journal_io.row_target(row)==target and _journal_io.row_moment(row)<=before, and returns the newest row's (action, actor.via, ts). _index_write_clause composes ' (last written by <action> via <via> at <ts>)' or ' (the write is not in the journal)' and is spliced once per commit (lazily, only when a non-pairing finding exists) into the breach text. plugins/audit/tests/test__invariants.py: added `_index_write_row` (writes a journal row via the real _journal_io.append, targeting docs/audit/audit-plan.json with a caller-chosen ts/action/via), a new `index_writes` build() parameter that appends such rows after the fixture's commits, and two new selftest cases - iv18g (three rows, two before the commit's committer time and one after; the breach names the NEWEST one-before, action audit.task.scope via orchestrator, and excludes both the older row and the after-commit one) and iv18h (only an after-commit row; the breach reads 'the write is not in the journal'). Ran python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__invariants.py --selftest: 123/123 passed. Ran python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --jobs 6 in the task tree: 334/334 files ok, 16021 cases, exit 0 (no file failed under load).
outcome.descriptive: An index-validity breach now names which journal-recorded command (or the absence of one) last wrote the manifest index before the offending commit, instead of leaving the operator to guess.

testsAdded: iv18g: an index-validity breach names the NEWEST journal row that wrote the index before the commit's committer time - not the oldest one, and not the one written AFTER it
iv18h: when no journal row targets the index AT OR BEFORE the commit, the breach says the write is not in the journal rather than naming the nearest row it could find
